title: Tacenta test-vector file
description: A set of known-answer or conformance vectors for one algorithm or protocol component. Primitive vectors come from public standards; each protocol vector file names whether its answers come from the Lean model or a recorded project-generated fixture. Byte strings are lowercase hex.

algorithm.description: The primitive or protocol component under test, e.g. hkdf-sha256 or double-ratchet.

source.description: Where the answers come from: a standards reference, a model revision, or the recorded method used for a project-generated fixture.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the file.

result.description: Whether the operation is expected to succeed. A valid vector carries output or fields. An invalid vector carries neither, and its input must be refused (in the three decoder files under vectors/malformed-input/, as a decode failure; in the persisted-state files, with the refusal it names; in the files under vectors/identity/, with the refusal it names, or with one of the refusals it lists as acceptable), with two exceptions: in vectors/post-quantum/erasure-decode.json, invalid means that the decoder, offered the listed codewords, holds no value, which is not a refusal; and in vectors/primitives/x25519.json, invalid means that the agreement is refused as non-contributory, because the peer's key is of low order and the output would be all zero (tacenta-test-vectors/README.md, Vector layouts).

inputs.description: Named inputs, each a lowercase hex string. Where a file's inputs are the fields of a format a protocol page specifies, each input is that field's encoded bytes, and the page says where an input's name differs from its field's. For the composite header (vectors/serialization/message-encoding.json and vectors/post-quantum/composite.json), tacenta-spec/protocol/message-format.md, Ratchet message, says that the input chunk_data is the field chunk, and that chunk_present, chunk_index and chunk_data together encode one optional codeword: when chunk_present is 00, the other two are its all-zero padding. The inputs and outputs of the erasure-code, persistence, protobuf and AEAD files, and of the three decoder files under vectors/malformed-input/, are laid out in tacenta-test-vectors/README.md, Vector layouts. In each decoder file the one input, encoding, is the bytes handed to the decoder, whole: in composite-header-decode.json a 102-byte composite header and nothing after it, in prekey-bundle-decode.json a whole prekey bundle, and in initial-message-decode.json a whole initial message. In the AEAD files (vectors/aead/), the input ad is what message-format.md, Authenticated encryption, calls AD: the whole associated data given to HMAC-SHA256, which for a ratchet message is already CONCAT(ad, header). A runner does not apply CONCAT to it. The identity-record files under vectors/identity/ (pair-digest.json, verification-number.json, identity-classification.json, identity-lookup.json and initiator-expectation.json) lay out their inputs there too: a list of keys is their 32-byte encodings concatenated, and a list of records is counted.

output.description: Expected output for a valid vector, lowercase hex. For the files tacenta-test-vectors/README.md, Vector layouts, describes, that section says what the output is.

refusal.description: Carried only by an invalid vector. Every invalid vector in vectors/persistence/ carries one except the erasure coders': ratchet-state, sparse-ratchet-state, triple-ratchet-state, braid-state, prekey-store-state and session-state. For stored bytes offered to a reader: which of the refusals tacenta-spec/protocol/session-persistence.md, Rejection, names the reader gives the input. wrong-version is an unrecognised version. short-or-malformed is everything else a reader refuses, a state its semantic rules exclude included, and is what every format but the session gives for those. incoherent is the prekey store's alone, for its signature rule, which the model cannot decide: signed-prekey-signature-does-not-verify is emitted only after the model has accepted and re-encoded the mutated bytes. inconsistent is the session's alone: Rejection distinguishes it from malformed because a stored session that is well-formed and canonical but cannot go on is the one case a storage layer could plausibly have written itself, so the session's semantic rules carry it and its field-by-field refusals do not. non-canonical is named by that section too, for the session and the prekey store, and is carried by no vector: a reader that accepts only canonical encodings can be offered one but never accepts one, so no vector generated from the model can record it. One prekey-store case is refused by tacenta-core as non-canonical and by the model as malformed, a v5 legacy_blocked list out of order or repeating an identifier; the page lets a reader report either (session-persistence.md, Legacy markers), so its vectors carry short-or-malformed. For operations whose last step is refused: counter-exhaustion names ChainExhausted at a counter ceiling; no-chain names the sparse ratchet's NoChain refusal for an epoch absent after retirement. invalid-identity-key is carried by every invalid vector of identity-key.json, bundle-admission.json and initial-message-admission.json under vectors/identity/: in identity-key.json the one input, key, is a 32-byte string that is not an identity key under the rule of tacenta-spec/protocol/identities-and-devices.md, Accepting a signed statement, check 6 (a non-canonical spelling included); in bundle-admission.json and initial-message-admission.json the input names an identity key that rule refuses, and the input is refused as an invalid identity key. A stored identity key that rule refuses is not this value: the persisted-state files give it the refusal of their format, inconsistent for the session and short-or-malformed for the prekey store. The identity-record files under vectors/identity/ (tacenta-spec/protocol/identities-and-devices.md, The identity pair digest; session-establishment.md, Records, expectations and attribution, and Sending the initial message) carry a refusal, or acceptable_refusals, on every invalid vector: decode-failure is a presented key that is not the canonical encoding of a curve public key, refused as DecodeEC refuses it; invalid-identity-key is a canonical presented key that the identity-key rule refuses; malformed-record is a record, or an initiator's expectation, that holds a non-canonical key, or an expectation of a known contact whose record is empty (MalformedRecord); unexpected-identity and retired-identity are a bundle's identity key that the initiator's expectation refuses (UnexpectedIdentity, RetiredIdentity). initiator-expectation.json also names the refusals of Sending the initial message that the expectation is ordered against: inconsistent-bundle is the presence check, non-canonical-key the canonical-key check of the bundle's curve keys, authentication-failure a prekey signature that does not verify, kem-input the KEM prekey's input checks, and non-contributory an agreement that is not contributory.

acceptable_refusals.description: Carried only by an invalid vector, in place of refusal, where a page lets an implementation report any one of several refusals: the input is refused with one of them, and a runner accepts any of them. The refusals are distinct. Used in vectors/identity/pair-digest.json for a pair of keys refused with different kinds, where identities-and-devices.md, The identity pair digest, says that either refusal conforms.

fields.description: For a valid vector with several named answers: each value is a lowercase hex string, with an integer encoded as its big-endian bytes. Carried instead of output. For a decoder, these are the values the input decodes to and a value reported absent is left out. For the full-session known answer, tacenta-test-vectors/README.md names every intermediate and resulting value. A runner must check that the names match as well as the values. The protobuf files (vectors/protobuf/) spell field names in snake_case where tacenta-spec/protocol/protobuf-profile.md spells them in camelCase: ratchet_key is ratchetKey, previous_counter is previousCounter, prekey_id is prekeyId, base_key is baseKey, identity_key is identityKey, registration_id is registrationId, signed_prekey_id is signedPrekeyId, and pq_prekey_id is pqPrekeyId. counter, ciphertext, pq, message and kem are spelled the same in both. Names are compared in the vectors' spelling. The identity-record files under vectors/identity/ lay out their fields in tacenta-test-vectors/README.md, Vector layouts.
